verdict.reasoning: Patient reports chest tightness and states duration: "my chest has been feeling really tight" and when asked how long: "for about... three hours now."

Symptoms are described as: "Yeah, like a little bit, um. Yeah, a little bit short of breath, not too bad." and "I'm feeling a bit wheezy, as well. Kind of cough , coughing". The doctor summarizes: "non-productive cough" and asks "Is the cough worse at night-time?"; patient replies: "it gets a little bit worse at night but, basically, just pretty consistent."

Doctor asks about exertion and rest: "are you short of breath at rest?". Patient: "I'm definitely not short of breath at rest" and adds "when I'm walking up stairs, I do feel like, I have a little bit, more short of breath than I would normally be."
Patient: "you know I had a cold last week... I had a sore throat, I had a runny nose..." and later: "I feel worse, but the runny nose isn't as bad any more" and "the cough's kind of stuck around."

Doctor clarifies: "you wouldn't say you've got chest pains? It's more of a tight chest, is it?" Patient: "No, not really pain, it's more like, tight. It just feels like sometimes, I can't get a full breath in, you know."

Patient confirms asthma: "Yeah, yeah, I have asthma". Regarding severe exacerbation: "when I was in high school, I had to have a tube put down my throat." Doctor paraphrases as staying in hospital for a few days with an asthma exacerbation, consistent with intubation in high school.
Patient: "I have like, a hayfever, you know, and some allergies just to dust, stuff like that."
Patient: "my mum has eczema, and my dad has asthma. , ohh, when I was young, I also had eczema. And I had a milk protein allergy, when I was young too."
Patient: "you know the um, uh, Ventolin. It's called uh, Salbutamol. I got that one" indicating use of a Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler.

Patient: "I have a steroid, a Clenil, Clenil inhaler." and later: "they ran out and I, I forgot to, go and grab the next one... About a week ago." Doctor confirms: "you haven't got any Clenil, or any Ventolin at the moment?" Patient: "Not with me right now, no, I ran out." This supports that he uses Clenil Modulite, ran out about a week ago, and has not used it for about a week.
When asked about drug allergies: "any drug allergies, that you know of?" Patient: "No, no, not allergic to anything. Just like, just the, dust and stuff, but nothing, no drugs."
Patient explicitly mentions: "some allergies just to dust, stuff like that."
Patient: "my mum has eczema".
Patient: "my dad has asthma."
On spacer use: Doctor: "Have you got one?" Patient: "I think I do, I have one somewhere." and earlier: "I don't, I don't really use it, to be honest" indicating he has a spacer but is not using it.

Doctor summarizes: "you've had this cold, so you've got wheezy with a cough... and you're short of breath" indicating an asthma attack. Patient notes recent cold last week and ongoing symptoms. Regarding medications: "I was away at uni last week, and I forgot to bring it with me, so I haven't really in the past week... they ran out" and doctor: "you haven't got any Clenil, or any Ventolin at the moment?" This supports an acute asthma exacerbation in the context of a recent URI and 1‑week lapse in inhaled corticosteroid and SABA use.

No SOB at rest: Patient: "I'm definitely not short of breath at rest". History of prior intubation in teenage years: "when I was in high school, I had to have a tube put down my throat." and age at event: "I think I was like seventeen. Sixteen maybe."
Doctor: "I think, what, the other thing I'd like to do is just give you a, dose of steroids. So this is, these are tablets which, um, you can take for five days. Uh, two tablets in the morning."

Doctor explains side effects: "they can make you, your mood change... Can give you, a high blood sugar... they can also cause rash, nausea, um, headaches" and frames this as side-effect counselling for the oral steroids.

Doctor: "send you these, the, some prescriptions for your, uh, inhalers, , ongoing... you can, once you get better from this asthma attack, you can, you can, use the Clenil Modulite in the morning, with Ventolin as a PRN. , so, a Ventolin when you need to, um, when you're getting wheezy."
Doctor: "the other thing I'd like to send you is a spacer" and then gives instructions: "couple of puffs to prime it, inside, breathing in and out, um, uh, for five or , five or ten breaths."
Doctor: "I might give you some time off work as well. You can self-certify first seven days, but uh, I think I would advise you just to, rest a little bit until you're feeling a bit better".

Safety net: "If you should start to use the Ventolin more than, uh, every three hours... it's a good idea to seek medical attention" and later: "Any deterioration in your symptoms, like worsening shortness of breath. Um, or just generally concerning symptoms, uh, pain in your chest tightness, uh, feeling light-headed. Uh, then, seek further medical attention anytime please."

Doctor: "I think what we can do is, is give you a prescription for, uh, some more of the inhalers. We can get that to you, within the hour, I would hope." indicating aim of delivery within approximately 1 hour.

Patient's goals: "probably getting my, inhalers would be helpful" and later: "Well I just wanna know that I'm OK... I just don't wanna have to get, um, that, that intubation again." This reflects desire for reassurance and prescriptions to avoid repeat intubation.
